Kalispel

Kalispel is a reading route into a people whose historical communities are connected with the Pend Oreille region of Washington, Idaho and Montana. Start with the Kalispel Tribe of Indians’ own account, then compare an older regional history that distinguishes Upper and Lower Kalispel contexts. This introduction does not treat every historical community as the same present government.

Read the sources [3] Kalispel Tribe of Indians [1] Northwest Power Planning Council; hosted by GovInfo

These are selected starting points. The full annotated collection, source perspectives, inspection limits and remaining research questions follow below. A starting guide is not an exhaustive history or community endorsement.

01

Identity and homelands

Kalispel homelands extend along the Pend Oreille River, Lake Pend Oreille, and Clark Fork region.

Read the sources [1] Northwest Power Planning Council; hosted by GovInfo

02

Historical context

Upper and Lower Kalispel communities experienced different nineteenth-century relocations. The Lower Kalispel reservation was established in 1914.

Read the sources [1] Northwest Power Planning Council; hosted by GovInfo

03

Living communities and further study

The Kalispel Tribe’s own news and cultural reporting provide a contemporary counterpart to government historical summaries.

Read the sources [2] Kalispel Tribe of Indians

04

People, places and distinct political paths

The older Tribal Briefing Book distinguishes Upper and Lower Kalispel communities and describes different responses to settlement and removal. Its Kalispel chapter places Lake Pend Oreille within this wider history. Because it combines historical narrative with dated administrative information, it is useful for framing questions rather than establishing current leadership, landholdings or legal rights. Original records and fuller community histories remain important next steps.

Read the sources [1] Northwest Power Planning Council; hosted by GovInfo

05

A community account of rebuilding

The Kalispel Tribe of Indians’ public story links the loss of land and limited economic opportunities with efforts to build housing, education and community services. It presents a 1991 vision statement as part of that history. Read those goals in their stated historical setting; they do not demonstrate that every aspiration was fulfilled or describe all Kalispel communities in the same way.

Read the sources [3] Kalispel Tribe of Indians

Tribal Briefing Book — Kalispel Tribe of Indians, selected pages ↗

Publication: Undated historical compilation; internal late-1990s references are not a verified publication date

Read the selected Kalispel historical narrative and the introduction to this older regional compilation. It distinguishes Upper and Lower Kalispel contexts. Dated administrative totals, officeholders, ceremonies and assertions about current legal rights are not adopted.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Introduction, PDF page 2 and selected narrative on printed/PDF pages 39–40 read; the Kalispel narrative begins at zero-based page 38. Other tribal chapters, fullvolume, underlying records and source images were not inspected. Its claim locating Albeni Falls Dam on the Kootenai River is erroneous and not repeated. End-of-century administrative listings are historical, not current.

Review recorded: October 27, 2026

Access note: Public GovInfo PDF actual selectable text inspected. Prior generic source card is explicitly upgraded with this documented review; URL and ID retained, publisher corrected from the earlier generic attribution.

Our Story ↗

Publication: Undated; access date is not a publication date

The Tribe’s own account connects history, community wellbeing and its relationship with the Pend Oreille country. The1991 vision is an aspiration, not proof that every goal was later realized.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Complete public main body lines 33–76 read, including historical hardship, the explicitly aspirational1991 vision statement and homeland/reservation narrative. Present totals, business counts, income, population and legal land status were not adopted.
